title: traffic-conditional throughput confidence fence and hysteresis rollback policy
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a traffic-conditioned throughput confidence fence for canaries; introduces hysteresis-driven rollback budget and dashboarding for throughput SLOs.
description: Context and motivation: We observed false-positive throughput regressions during short-lived traffic bursts and cross-tenant traffic spikes when running canaries. This PR introduces a traffic-conditional throughput confidence fence: a statistical estimator that normalizes throughput delta signals by recent traffic modality and owns a hysteresis rollback budget so transient spikes do not immediately trigger rollbacks. The feature is intended to reduce noisy canary failures while keeping the fail-fast property for sustained regressions. Implementation summary: 1) Introduced a lightweight traffic-modality classifier that tags windows as steady, bursty, or ramping based on rate derivatives and per-cohort heatmaps. 2) Added a Bayesian throughput delta estimator that conditions on modality and produces a calibrated confidence interval for observed throughput change. 3) Implemented a hysteresis-backed rollback budget: the fence exposes a budget that decays with confirmed regressions and replenishes slowly; rollbacks only occur when inferred regression exceeds confidence threshold and budget allows. 4) Integrated guard into canary orchestrator: policy knobs (sensitivity, lookback, budget-rate) are plumbed through canary config; automatic fallback to conservative rules for low-traffic tenants. 5) Telemetry and dashboarding: new metrics (throughput_delta_ci_lower, throughput_confidence, modality_tag, rollback_budget) + console panels and alert rules. Tests and verification: unit tests for estimator math, deterministic simulation harness that replays historical traffic traces (production and synthetic) to validate false-positive reduction, and an end-to-end integration run in perf-canary staging. Backwards compatibility: feature is opt-in at the canary policy level; default remains previous detector. Rollout plan: feature flagged; staged rollout to internal tenants for 2 weeks, then opt-in for 25% of external canaries before full opt-in. Related items: ENG-1967 (reduce noisy canary rollbacks), ENG-2011 (hysteresis policy design).

review_comments: Arjun Kapoor: Could the modality classifier be driven from existing rate metrics instead of adding a new collector? Concern about additional cardinality.

Author (Maya Chen): We reuse existing rate streams where possible; added a thin collector only for per-cohort derivatives to avoid increasing global metric cardinality. Updated docs to explain storage impact.
Sophie Alvarez: The hysteresis budget parameters look sensitive; can we expose safe defaults and a debug endpoint to inspect budget state?
Author (Maya Chen): Added a read-only /canary/debug/budget endpoint and set conservative defaults (replenish=0.05/min, drain_threshold=0.95) in config. Included guidance in rollout notes.
Liam O'Neill: Integration test flaked once on CI due to timing; recommend switching the sim to deterministic time base.
Author (Maya Chen): Switched the sim harness to a mocked clock and re-recorded the golden traces; CI stabilized.
